name: Premier Energies Ltd
title: Premier Energies Ltd - 544238 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Premier Energies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR2,508 crores, PAT up 53% to INR472 crores at an 18.8% margin.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q1 revenue and profit, with EBITDA up 27% to INR759 crores at a 30.3% margin and PAT up 53% to INR472 crores; results include consolidation of the 51% stake in Transcon. The 5.6 GW Seetharampur module plant is operational, while the 7 GW TOPCon cell line is in late commissioning with trial runs expected later in August. Order wins were INR3,011 crores in the quarter, taking the total order book to INR15,000 crores including transformers. Management said the ALMM extension to December triggered a surge in non-DCR module orders, while DCR is sold out through FY28 per management.

financial_highlights.value: INR18 crores (17% PAT margin, 27% EBITDA margin)
About INR1,500 crores (INR1,250 crores solar, INR250 crores Transcon)

segments.name: Solar cells and modules
segments.commentary: Cells were about 24% of Q1 revenue and about 58% of the order book per analyst figures cited on the call. Modules are mainly DCR; management said DCR is sold out and selling only for FY28, while non-DCR realisations softened on oversupply.

segments.name: Transformers (Transcon, 51%)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue INR110 crores, PAT INR18 crores; management expects business to roughly treble over three years, with transformer capacity going from 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28. Last year's revenue was about INR400 crores.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Land acquired and construction started on a 12 GWh plan, with Phase 1 at 6 GWh; technology partner for containerised solution expected to be finalised in 2-3 months.

guidance_outlook: Margins guided at 29-30% (plus or minus 100-150 bps), supported by 7 GW cell line, transformer scale-up and ingot-wafer backward integration.
First revenue from 7 GW cell line targeted in September; about 50-60% utilisation by November; at least 70% targeted by March quarter.
Depreciation expected to rise to about INR240-250 crores per quarter in Q3 and Q4 FY27 as Seetharampur and Naidupeta lines are capitalised.
Transformer revenue ramp expected to be slightly below analyst's INR600-700 crore FY27 estimate given certification and type-testing lead times; revenue expected to rise substantially over two years.
Management expects at least 40-45% of the INR15,000 crore order book to execute in FY28.
Management sees no concrete plan to raise primary capital in the near future; enabling resolution is precautionary.
Europe export office being opened; US cell manufacturing JV expected to produce output in 24-30 months.
capex_capacity: 5.6 GW fully automated solar module plant at Seetharampur is operational.
7 GW TOPCon cell line (Naidupeta/Tirupati) in advanced commissioning; trial runs expected later in August 2026; first revenue targeted in September.
Telangana operational cell plants ran at a record 92% utilisation in Q1.
Transformer capacity to rise from 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28; ingot-wafer lines under way.
BESS 12 GWh plan with 6 GWh Phase 1 under construction.
demand_pricing: Analyst-cited estimates: about 12 GW of solar capacity added in Q1 CY/FY across market; management expects about 6-8 GW AC (over 8 GW possible) of KUSUM installations over next nine months, with blended DC overloading of 1.2-1.25x, plus 1.2-1.3 GW per quarter from PM Surya Ghar.

Non-DCR orders surged after the ALMM extension to December; management says non-DCR business is not profitable currently with over 200-250 GW module capacity against about 30 GW non-DCR demand, though prices improved slightly for the coming quarter.
DCR module realisations stable: Surya Ghar about 24-24.5 cents/W, KUSUM about 22 cents/W, C&I slightly lower; no change expected over 12-15 months as orders are booked.
Cell pricing (mono-PERC) stable; long-term cell contracts have variable wafer, silver and FX pass-through. Most orders are USD-linked.

Management said the cell-to-DCR-module mix will shift steadily over the next 18-24 months; cell sales expected at about 50-50 internal vs external split historically, skewing to internal use as ALMM Phase 2 and DCR demand grow.
US minimum import price proposal on cells and modules cited as making US manufacturing attractive; Europe tenders in Italy and France and expected in Germany.

qa_highlights.question: How much DC overloading should be assumed for PM KUSUM, and what is the demand outlook for the next nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended overloading of 1.2-1.25x (KUSUM B at 1.0x, KUSUM C at 1.3-1.5x). Management expects about 1.2-1.3 GW per quarter of rooftop and 6-8 GW AC (possibly more than 8 GW) of KUSUM over nine months; total about 23-24 GW DC over nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why sell cells rather than convert them into DCR modules and capture the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy cell contracts signed earlier must be honoured; as the 7 GW cell line starts, DCR module output will rise and cell sales will fall. Q1 module orders were mostly for modules.

qa_highlights.question: Will C&I demand be deferred by the ALMM extension, and is DCR capacity blocked?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said C&I clients are already blocking capacity for FY28 and are not deferring; DCR is sold out with FY28 sales underway.

qa_highlights.question: Is 29-30% EBITDA margin sustainable over the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets maintaining 29-30% (plus or minus 100-150 bps), citing 7 GW cell line, transformer scale-up and backward integration into ingot-wafer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the transformer revenue ramp for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the initial ramp to be slightly below the analyst's INR600-700 crore FY27 estimate; business to treble over three years versus last year's INR400 crores; margins targeted slightly above the historical 15% EBITDA / 8-10% PAT cycle average.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses and employee costs jump sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to advance hiring for Seetharampur and Naidupeta, power costs of Seetharampur built up before July ramp-up, and corporate hiring tied to acquisitions. Per-GW manpower at Seetharampur is expected about 40% lower.

risks_watch: Execution timing on the 7 GW TOPCon cell line: trial runs slated for later in August, first revenue targeted for September, and 50-60% utilisation by November; at least 70% targeted by the March quarter.

Non-DCR module pricing and profitability: management said non-DCR business is not profitable currently against over 200 GW of module capacity versus about 30 GW of non-DCR demand, with slight price improvement expected for the coming quarter.

Transformer ramp risk: management said FY27 revenue will be slightly below the analyst's INR600-700 crore estimate due to certification and type-testing lead times; watch transformer revenue against the 16.25 GVA FY28 capacity target.

Depreciation step-up to about INR240-250 crores per quarter in Q3 and Q4 FY27, and other expenses and employee costs rising sharply ahead of capacity ramp; watch whether the 29-30% EBITDA margin guidance (plus or minus 100-150 bps) holds.

BESS technology partner expected in 2-3 months, with management going slow pending government guidelines on non-tariff barrier rules; US cell JV output expected in 24-30 months; Europe export office being opened.
key_quotes: So, we are quite confident that we will be able to maintain healthy margins.
DCR is, we are sold out. So, you know, we are selling now only for FY28 now.
As we speak, I can confirm that there is no concrete plan to raise any primary capital in the near future.
So, in general, we have said in the past that we want to maintain a business split of 50-50 for our cell production: 50% to be sold externally and 50% to be consumed internally.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand, DCR sell-out and margin guidance of 29-30%, but cautious and sometimes evasive on segment economics: it declined to give cell versus module margins by product and would not quantify the cell spread. It was also deliberately slow on BESS manufacturing and on US and Europe manufacturing, pending government guidance.

adds.what: 7 GW TOPCon cell line (Naidupeta/Tirupati) in advanced commissioning; first revenue targeted September
Transformer capacity 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28
BESS 12 GWh plan, 6 GWh Phase 1 under construction

growth.why: Management guides margins held at 29-30% and transformer revenue to treble over three years, with 7 GW cell line first revenue in September (50-60% utilisation by November, 70%+ by March quarter) and INR15,000 crore order book with 40-45% executing in FY28; no explicit total revenue growth percentage guided, and non-DCR overcapacity (200+ GW vs ~30 GW demand) is a headwind.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides operating EBITDA margin held at 29-30% (plus or minus 100-150 bps) with Q1 at 30.3%, supported by the 7 GW cell line ramp (50-60% utilisation by November, 70%+ by March quarter), transformer scale-up and ingot-wafer backward integration; however depreciation rises to INR240-250 crore per quarter in Q3-Q4 FY27 and non-DCR pricing is weak.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The 7 GW TOPCon cell line at Naidupeta is in advanced commissioning with trial runs in late August and first revenue targeted in September, while transformer capacity rises from 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28 and the 6 GWh BESS Phase 1 is under construction.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Telangana cell plants ran at a record 92% utilisation, DCR is sold out through FY28, the order book is INR15,000 crore with 40-45% executing in FY28, and KUSUM plus rooftop demand is 6-8 GW AC plus 1.2-1.3 GW per quarter over nine months; the 7 GW cell line ramp to 50-60% by November adds volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex in Q1 was about INR1,500 crore and utilisation is 92%, but the 7 GW cell line, transformer expansion and 12 GWh BESS plan are already under way, and management is slow on BESS and US/Europe manufacturing pending government guidance; new announcements depend on that guidance.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held margin guidance at 29-30% and guided transformer FY27 revenue slightly below the INR600-700 crore analyst estimate, so there is no sign of a raise in the near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Depreciation steps up to INR240-250 crore per quarter, other expenses and employee costs rose sharply, non-DCR capacity of 200-250 GW against about 30 GW demand is unprofitable, and transformer revenue is guided below the INR600-700 crore estimate.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: BESS technology partner in 2-3 months; Europe export office
rows.why: The BESS containerised solution partner is expected to be finalised in 2-3 months on a 12 GWh plan with 6 GWh Phase 1 under construction, though management is going slow pending government guidelines.

rows.label: Order book INR15,000 crore; 40-45% executes in FY28
rows.why: Order inflow was INR3,011 crore in Q1 and management expects at least 40-45% of the INR15,000 crore book (about INR6,000-6,750 crore) to execute in FY28.

rows.label: Non-DCR module oversupply pressure
rows.why: Non-DCR business is unprofitable against 200-250 GW of module capacity versus about 30 GW demand, and only a slight price improvement is expected for the coming quarter, while DCR realisations (Surya Ghar 24-24.5 cents/W, KUSUM about 22 cents/W) are stable for 12-15 months.

rows.label: US cell JV and Europe export office
rows.when: 24-30 months for US JV output; Europe office being opened no
rows.why: US cell JV output is expected in 24-30 months and Europe tenders in Italy and France are live, but management is deliberately slow pending government guidance on US and Europe manufacturing.

tone.note: Management was confident on DCR sell-out, 92% cell utilisation and the 29-30% margin guide, but cautious and evasive on cell versus module economics and BESS/US manufacturing; analysts pushed on margin sustainability, the transformer ramp and the sharp rise in other expenses and employee costs.
